title: Deacons
hook: since 1967 permanent deacons, often married, serve in the Latin Church

segments.voice: Yesterday, religious life: the evangelical counsels, and a rich young man who went away sad. Your line was three vows. What did you give away, or set aside, or let someone else choose? Day one thousand four hundred ten.

Sunday morning. A man in an alb steps up to the ambo to proclaim the Gospel. His stole doesn't hang straight down like the priest's: it crosses his chest from one shoulder to the opposite hip, like a sash. He reads, then he preaches, and somewhere in the homily he mentions his grandson's soccer game. In the third pew, his wife rolls her eyes and smiles. On Monday he'll be back at his job, and on Thursday evening he'll be at the county jail, leading a Bible study. He is ordained, and he is married, and he is neither a priest nor a man on his way to becoming one. Today, deacons.
screen: `A STOLE WORN LIKE A SASH.` → `HIS WIFE IN THE THIRD PEW.` → `ORDAINED, BUT NOT A PRIEST.`

segments.voice: A deacon is a servant. The Catechism calls Christ himself the deacon, or servant, of all. In Mark's Gospel, Jesus says it of himself, in the Douay-Rheims: "For the Son of man also is not come to be ministered unto: but to minister, and to give his life a redemption for many." To minister there means to serve, to wait on. The Acts of the Apostles tells how the office began. The Greek-speaking widows in Jerusalem were being overlooked in the daily distribution of food. The apostles asked the community to choose seven men full of the Spirit and wisdom, and laid hands on them for this work. Stephen was one of them. Tradition sees in them the first deacons. By the time Paul writes to Philippi, he greets the church "with the bishops and deacons." Next, what a deacon does. The Catechism lists it: assisting the bishop and priests at the Eucharist, giving communion, witnessing and blessing marriages, proclaiming the Gospel and preaching, presiding at funerals, and giving himself to works of charity. He does not consecrate the Eucharist or hear confessions. He is ordained, the Catechism says, not for priesthood but for service. Then the two kinds. Men on the road to priesthood are ordained deacons first. But the Second Vatican Council asked that the diaconate be restored in the Latin Church as a permanent rank, open to men of mature age, including married men. So the deacon at the ambo is part of something old and something renewed at once: a married man, ordained to serve.
screen: `CHRIST, THE SERVANT OF ALL.` · `SEVEN CHOSEN TO SERVE THE WIDOWS.` · `GOSPEL, ALTAR, CHARITY.` · `RESTORED AS A PERMANENT RANK.` · then, large: `NOT TO BE MINISTERED UNTO, BUT TO MINISTER.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: thank a deacon. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind a deacon you know, or one you've seen at a baptism, a funeral or a Sunday Mass. If you don't know one, think of anyone whose work is to serve quietly: a nurse's aide, a cafeteria worker, a volunteer at a food pantry. Picture their hands at work. If you pray, you can thank God for them and ask strength for their service. If you don't, simply hold them in mind and wish them a good day's work. The bell holds the time.
Deacons. Men ordained not for priesthood but for service: to proclaim the Gospel, assist at the altar and serve in charity, and in the Latin Church today, including married men. Today's word.

Your line: servants. Today, wait on someone the way a server does: refill a glass, clear a plate, hold a door, and don't mention it. If you know a deacon, thank him. Day one thousand four hundred ten.

howItsDone: Catholic deacons are ordained by a bishop. At Mass they proclaim the Gospel, may preach, and assist at the altar; they also baptize, witness marriages, lead funeral rites and serve in works of charity. In the Latin Church, permanent deacons may be married men who keep their jobs and families.

trapdoor: what you thought: a deacon is a priest in training.
what it means: a man ordained to serve: the Gospel, the altar and the poor. some go on to priesthood; permanent deacons don't.
what a scholar hears: the Catechism's Christ the deacon, or servant, of all (CCC 1570); the seven of Acts 6; Lumen Gentium 29, restoring the diaconate as a permanent rank open to married men.

notes: Douay-Rheims wording of Mark 10:45 and Philippians 1:1: confirm.
The index's 'since 1967' (Paul VI, Sacrum Diaconatus Ordinem) is not stated; the script says the Council asked for the restoration. Confirm whether the date should be added with that document cited.
Acts 6 paraphrased (Hellenist widows, seven men, laying on of hands); 'tradition sees in them the first deacons' since Acts doesn't use the noun 'deacon' for them. Confirm.

CCC 1569–1571 (ordained 'not unto the priesthood but unto the ministry'; tasks listed; permanent diaconate open to married men) paraphrased; confirm. 'He does not consecrate the Eucharist or hear confessions' is inferred from Church law (only priests); confirm.
Deacon's stole worn over the left shoulder and fastened at the right side: described as 'like a sash'; confirm.
Hook: the deacon at a jail Bible study is an illustrative scene.
Editor: cut the Greek etymology claims; servant meaning now tied to CCC 1570; 'often married' softened to 'including married men'; practice ending changed so it doesn't repeat yesterday's.
